title: Rep. Waters calls for 25th Amendment to be used against Trump - Conservative Institute
content: U.S. Representative Maxine Waters (D‑CA) has urged the use of the Twenty‑Fifth Amendment to remove President Donald Trump, citing Trump’s recent removal of Federal Reserve Board member Lisa Cook as evidence of executive overreach.  Waters said, 'I want, even though I know it may not happen, the cabinet that he’s appointed, a bunch of his sycophants who probably won’t do what I would recommend,' and called for an aggressive move to declare Trump unfit for office.  She described the situation as 'extraordinarily dangerous' and a 'makings of a dictator who is trying to control the entire economy.'  Waters’ remarks were made on MSNBC and echoed in a Conservative Institute article that framed the issue as a threat to democracy.  The article also referenced the legal battle between Trump and Cook over her removal and explained the procedural steps of the Twenty‑Fifth Amendment, concluding that Waters’ stance is unlikely to succeed.

title: The 25th Amendment and Trump: could it actually work?
content: The 25th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, designed to ensure presidential continuity, includes Section 4—a provision that allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to declare the president 'unable to discharge the powers and duties of his office,' thereby transferring power to the Vice President as acting president. This provision has never been invoked in U.S. history. Illinois Governor JB Pritzker became the first sitting governor to publicly call for its use against President Donald Trump during his second term, alleging Trump suffers from dementia and emulates Vladimir Putin’s tactics. The amendment’s framers deliberately left 'inability' undefined, sparking debate over whether it applies only to physical incapacity or can include mental decline or erratic judgment. Despite escalating political rhetoric, the amendment’s practical application remains nearly impossible: it requires the Vice President’s cooperation, and there is no indication Vice President JD Vance would support such action against the president who appointed him. The Reagan administration came closest to invoking Section 4 after President Reagan was shot in 1981, but did not proceed. The amendment’s high threshold—requiring a majority of the Cabinet and congressional approval—was intended to prevent political manipulation. Critics argue that invoking it for political disagreements undermines its purpose, while supporters see it as a vital safeguard. Trump himself has weaponized the debate, warning that the amendment will 'come back to haunt Joe Biden.' Ultimately, the 25th Amendment remains a constitutional emergency measure, designed for extreme circumstances, not partisan conflict, and its continued existence serves as a critical, though rarely used, check on presidential power.

title: Can Trump be removed under the 25th Amendment?
content: The article examines renewed calls to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove President Donald Trump from office, following his recent remarks to military leaders in which he suggested cities like Chicago could serve as 'training grounds for our military.' Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker publicly urged the invocation of the 25th Amendment, stating that Trump's comments indicate cognitive decline and resemble tactics used by Russian President Vladimir Putin. Pritzker called Trump's actions 'insane' and claimed 'there is something genuinely wrong with this man.' The call was echoed by Democratic Congressman Eric Swalwell, who tweeted '25TH AMENDMENT!' during Trump's speech. Former military officials and veterans condemned the remarks as 'authoritarian and un-American,' with Ret. Army General Barry McCaffrey describing the address as 'one of the most bizarre, unsettling events I've ever encountered.' White House spokeswoman Abigail Jackson dismissed Pritzker as 'a slob of a governor' and mocked his mental state, suggesting he was 'hangry.' The article notes that the 25th Amendment has been used only for temporary transfers of power during medical procedures—such as Ronald Reagan’s 1985 colon cancer surgery, George W. Bush’s two colonoscopies, and Joe Biden’s 2021 procedure—never for removal. To remove a president, the vice president and a majority of the cabinet must jointly declare the president unable to discharge duties, or a disability review panel must be established with congressional approval. The president can challenge the declaration, but Congress has 21 days to decide with a two-thirds vote in both chambers. Despite past calls to invoke the amendment against Trump after January 6, 2021, and against Biden after reports on his mental fitness, such action remains politically improbable due to Trump’s strong support within the Republican Party and his Cabinet, including Vice President JD Vance, who would need to agree to removal.

title: Democrats call for 25th Amendment against Trump: What is it, what happens if it is invoked?
content: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker called for the invocation of the 25th Amendment to remove President Donald Trump from office, following Trump's remarks on October 1, 2025, in which he suggested using cities like Chicago as 'training grounds for our military' and claimed he would 'go into Chicago very soon.' Pritzker compared Trump to Russian President Vladimir Putin, stating that Trump's comments indicate 'something genuinely wrong' with him and suggesting he may be suffering from dementia. He asserted, 'There is something genuinely wrong with this man, and the 25th Amendment ought to be invoked.' This marks the first time Pritzker has publicly called for Trump's removal. The 25th Amendment addresses presidential succession and disability, stating that if the president is unable to discharge the powers and duties of the office, the Vice President becomes acting president. In this case, Vice President JD Vance would assume the role of acting president if the amendment were invoked. This is not the first time the 25th Amendment has been proposed for Trump—Senator Chuck Schumer previously called for its invocation after the January 6 Capitol insurrection, stating, 'This president should not hold office one day longer.'

title: "Trump 2028" talk is ramping up among Republicans
content: Talk of Donald Trump running for a third presidential term in 2028 has intensified among Republicans. Steve Bannon, a former senior adviser to Trump, claimed there are 'many different alternatives' to allow Trump to appear on the ballot despite the 22nd Amendment, which prohibits any person from being elected president more than twice. Bannon emphasized that such efforts would be legal and supported by a broad segment of the American public, though he did not specify the methods. Constitutional law expert James Sample from Hofstra University stated that the 22nd Amendment is 'clear and unequivocal,' and that any attempt to circumvent it—such as a 'false-pretense ticket' where Vice President JD Vance would step down to allow Trump to assume office—would be legally dubious and unlikely to gain public acceptance. Representative Randy Fine of Florida has called for repealing the 22nd Amendment, arguing that Trump's leadership is unparalleled. Trump himself has given mixed signals: in March 2025, he said he was 'not joking' about a third term and that 'methods' exist, but in August 2024 he stated he would 'probably not' run again. Repealing the amendment would require a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate and ratification by three-quarters of state legislatures—currently considered politically unfeasible. The 'Third Term Project' and Republican Representative Andy Ogles have also promoted constitutional amendments to allow a third term. Despite these efforts, experts agree the legal and political barriers are insurmountable, and any attempt would likely face immediate legal challenges.

title: UNBREAKING VIDEO –  Maxine Waters says it’s time to declare the 25th amendment – The Right Scoop
content: The article reports that Maxine Waters has publicly stated it is time to invoke the 25th Amendment to remove President Trump from office, citing his decision to fire Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve as the reason. According to the piece, Waters said, 'It’s time to declare the 25th amendment' and 'remove President Trump from office' because of Cook’s dismissal. The article, published on therightscoop.com on August 30 2025 11:24, uses sensational language such as 'corrupt and despicable' to describe Waters and frames the claim as a political attack. The piece is clearly political in nature, presenting a one‑sided argument without counter‑perspectives, and is designed to provoke a strong emotional response from readers.

title: What Is the 25th Amendment and Can It Remove Trump From Office?
content: Democrats, led by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, are calling for the invocation of the 25th Amendment to remove President Donald Trump from office following his controversial suggestion that cities like Chicago could be used as 'training grounds' for the U.S. military. The 25th Amendment outlines procedures for presidential succession and removal, but its invocation against Trump is considered unlikely due to strong support for him within his administration. The call comes amid rising political tensions and inflammatory rhetoric. According to TimesNow, the article was published on October 02, 2025, at 00:57.

title: Trump history 2025: Take a visual tour of our images and videos of Donald Trump and family
content: In 2025, Donald Trump is serving his second term as President of the United States, having returned to the White House. His family dynamics have evolved: Barron Trump is a college freshman at NYU, Ivanka Trump has stepped back from politics to focus on family life in Florida, and Donald Trump Jr. remains politically active, lobbying for Vice President JD Vance. The family publicly united to mourn conservative activist Charlie Kirk, with tributes from Ivanka, Eric, and Tiffany. Melania Trump maintains a low public profile but made select appearances during the campaign and inauguration. The Trump family continues to play symbolic and strategic roles in Trump’s presidency and public image. The family resides permanently in Palm Beach, Florida, following Donald Trump’s announcement on October 31, 2019, that he would make Mar-a-Lago his permanent residence. Mar-a-Lago, dubbed the 'Southern White House' during his presidency, remains central to the family’s life. Donald Trump is an avid golfer, with a documented history of playing golf multiple times a year. Barron Trump has lived in Manhattan, the White House, and Mar-a-Lago. Eric Trump’s wife, Lara Yunaska Trump, has been active in politics, serving as RNC chair and Fox News host. Vanessa Trump, former wife of Donald Trump Jr., has five children with him and lives in Jupiter, Florida. Viktor Knavs, grandfather of Barron Trump, was married to Amalija, Melania’s mother, who died in January 2024. The 41st Nicklaus Junior Championship took place on June 23–24 at Tequesta Country Club in Florida.

title: Trump migration policy struck down by judge - Taipei Times
content: A US District Court Judge, Jia Cobb, blocked the Trump administration’s expanded use of expedited removal, a procedure that had previously been limited to migrants detained near the Mexican border who had entered the US within the prior two weeks. The expansion, which applied to migrants who had been in the US for up to two years, was halted on August 30, 2025. Cobb warned that the broadened use could lead to people being 'erroneously' deported without due process, noting that 'the group of people the Government is now subjecting to expedited removal have long since entered our country.' She also said the government’s argument that illegal entrants are entitled to no Fifth Amendment process is 'truly startling' and would put 'everyone' at risk. The ruling was brought by Make The Road New York, a migrant‑rights group. Cobb, appointed by former President Joe Biden, said the court was not questioning the constitutionality of the expedited removal statute or its longstanding border application. The decision follows a series of court rulings that have limited President Trump’s mass‑deportation program, which he had campaigned on.
